sentences.text:
The petitioners in OP(MV) No. 877/2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Irinjalakkuda is the appellant herein.
The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

The petitioners filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained on account of the accident that occurred on 27.10.2007.
2.

According to the petitioner, the accident was occurred while the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KL-13/Q4295 through NH 47 in the sector Thrissur- Chalakkudy.

When he reached near the Thupankavu bridge at Nellayi the Car bearing Reg. No.
KL-26/4542 driven by the 2nd respondent over took the motorcycle negligently resulting to hit against the petitioner 2025:KER:8674 whereby the petitioner fell down to the road and sustained with injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the them, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.
8,35,000/- limited to Rs.6,00,000/-.
4. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained exparte.

The 3rd respondent filed a written statement,
admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the motorcycle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 to 3 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A11 and X1.
B1 Policy was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,15,480/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

sentences.text:
Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

9. Heard Sri. P.V. Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, Sri. P. Jacob Mathew,
learned Counsel appearing for the 3 rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the motorcycle, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioners produced Ext.A2, copy of the charge sheet involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the light of the above charge sheet, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.

Therefore,
the 3rdrespondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
11. The petitioners was aged 28 on the date of accident on 27.10.2007.
According to him he was working Leela Hotels, Bangalore 2025:KER:8674 getting a monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-.
The tribunal fixed his income at Rs.3,500/-
However, he has not produced any documents to prove his salary during the period of accident.
He has produced Ext.A10 Diploma in Hotel Management Certificate to prove that he was working in a hotel.
However, though he produced Ext. A10 Diploma in Certificate along with sufficient proof, yet he could not prove that he was working in Hotel Leela as claimed by him.

12. Therefore, by virtue of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236], even the notional income of a Coolie during the year 2007 will come to Rs.6,000/-.

Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236]

sentences.text: However, considering the fact that the petitioner in diploma holder in hotel management and aged 28.
I hold that his notional income is to be fixed at a sum more than that of a coolie during the allowed period.
Considering the fact I hold that notional income can be fixed at Rs.7,500/-.
13. Ext.X1 is the disability certificate issued by the medical board constituted by the Superintendent Medical College Hospital, Thrissur showing that his permanent physical disability is 7%.
The tribunal accepted the same and pass award on the basis that he had 7% 2025:KER:8674 permanent physical disability.
It was argued by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent that since there is no evidence to show that the petitioners future income is affected by the injury sustained by him.
Addition towards future prospects cannot be awarded.
He has also made up on the decision of Single Bench of this Court in Sarath vs. Prasanth [2024 (4) KLT 439].

In the above decision the learned Single Judge observed that:

sentences.text: "The component of 'loss of future prospects' also has to be factored in a case of serious injury resulting in permanent disablement, which ultimately has a bearing on the reduced earning capacity.

The crucial factor which has to be taken into consideration is to assess as to whether the permanent disability has any adverse effect on the earning capacity of the injured".
14.
From Ext.X1, it can be seen that because of the injuries the petitioner suffered out of the curt injury of the femoral condyle and the cable graft of sural nerve done for femoral nerve injury.

The result of the examination made by the medical board noted in Ext.X1 are the following:
"They have noted sensory loss of (R) medial side and medial side of leg, skin break down medial side of leg and creps on (R) knee.
They have noted that the miniscal injury to be ruled 2025:KER:8674 out.
The disability was assessed under the Mc.Bride's Scale for the sensory loss, for skin damage, quadrieps patella femoral arthritis weakening and bodily femoral arthritis to a total of 7%".
15. In the above circumstances I find no merits in the argument that the injury sustained by the petitioner and the disability suffered by him will affect his future prospects.
In the above circumstances, 40% of the income is liable to be added towards future prospects and the multiplier to be applied is 17.
Therefore, the loss of disability will come to Rs. 1,49,940/-.
16. Towards loss of earnings the tribunal has awarded Rs.17,500/- @3,500 for 5 months.
Since his notional income is fixed at Rs.7,500/- is entitled to get a sum of Rs.37,500/- (7500x5) towards loss of earning.
Towards pain and suffering the tribunal has awarded only Rs.20,000/-.
Similarly there is loss of amenities the tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/-.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the disability suffered by him on account of the injuries, I hold that compensation awarded on the head pain and suffering, loss of amenities are on the lesser side enhanced Rs.50,000/- each.
Towards extra nourishment the tribunal has awarded only 2025:KER:8674 Rs.500/-.
The petitioner was treated as inpatient for 25 days.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitoiner and the disability certificate on account of the injuries I hold that compensation awarded on the head extra nourishment is on the lesser side and hence it is enhanced Rs.10,000/-.
No alteration is required on other heads as compensation awarded on other heads appears reasonable.
The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- on the head loss of future prospects, it is not required as 40% of the income was already added towards future prospects in his notional income.
Therefore the above Rs.5,000/- is to be deducted.
17. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

18. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,12,000/-
(Rupees Four Lakh Twelve Thousand Only), as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
